[IRET.25.4.1] `DS_RETE_EXPR_NOW` nodes read the held wall-clock sample
([IRET.14.1]). The sample does not change between two sample points
([LTIM.2.8.4]), so nothing is cached and every encounter in a pump returns
one value. That is how [LTIM.2.1.3]'s activation atomicity is delivered.

idris.name: iret_25_4_1__fire_reads
idris.note: What `k` encounters of NOW nodes in one firing see under the held sample: each is `Now` evaluated by TwoClocks.idr's held reader, the count of source calls threaded through as that module threads it, so a call would be visible in the count.

idris.name: iret_25_4_1__fire_reads_held
idris.note: ONE FIRING SEES ONE VALUE AND CALLS NOTHING: `k` encounters see `k` copies of the held wall value and the count of source calls is what it was, for every sample, every count of encounters and every call count.

idris.name: iret_25_4_1__now_node
idris.note: A NOW node: a field read of the held sample's wall component. No clock function and no cache -- the clause's 'read the held wall-clock sample', as the one function it is.

idris.name: iret_25_4_1__one_value_per_pump
idris.note: EVERY ENCOUNTER IN A PUMP RETURNS ONE VALUE: for every sample, every list of firings with any counts of encounters, and every call count, each firing sees copies of the held wall value and the source is called not once. 'Nothing is cached': there is nothing to cache, the value being the sample's.

idris.name: iret_25_4_1__per_fire_pump
idris.note: A pump under the refused reading: every firing starts cold and reads the source at its first encounter. Partial for the reason `iret_25_4_1__per_fire_reads` is.

idris.name: iret_25_4_1__per_fire_reads
idris.note: THE REFUSED READING: a per-fire cache with a clock read at the firing's first encounter. Partial because it models a reading the clause does not admit; kept so that what is ruled out is computed beside what is required.

idris.name: iret_25_4_1__per_fire_reads_twice
idris.note: TWO FIRINGS IN ONE PUMP READ TWO VALUES UNDER THE REFUSED READING, from a source that moves at every call -- 0 then 1, the source called twice -- where the held sample gives both firings the one value and the source is called not once. Computed; the clause's 'so nothing is cached and every encounter in a pump returns one value', by the engine that caches per fire.

idris.name: iret_25_4_1__pump_reads
idris.note: A pump: its firings, each with its count of NOW encounters, all under the pump's one held sample -- a pump begins with a sample and takes no other ([LTIM.2.8.4]). What every firing's encounters see, and the count after.

idris.name: iret_25_4_1__pump_reads_cons
idris.note: One firing of a pump, unfolded: the first firing's reads, then the rest of the pump from the count the first left. By computation; a step for the theorem below.
